title: Repaired FF3 Security at N^(3/2) Queries
summary: Lower-query security results leave the repaired FF3-style construction's security unresolved in the query regime relevant to its four-round attack.

formal_statement.body: The repaired FF3-style Feistel construction, obtained by shortening FF3's tweak and concatenating the round index rather than XORing it, has security results only for lower query regimes; those results say nothing when $q\sim N^{3/2}$, the regime relevant to the four-round attack. The unresolved task is to characterize the construction's security when $q\sim N^{3/2}$ queries are available.

scope.domain: Security of a repaired FF3-style Feistel construction for format-preserving encryption.
parameters: q, the number of available queries
N, the parameter governing the query regime
scope.unresolved_remainder: Characterize the repaired construction's security when the available query count is approximately N to the three-halves power.

citations.label: Breaking the FF3 Format-Preserving Encryption Standard over Small Domains

progress.summary: The source presents security results for the repaired construction only in lower-query regimes. It explicitly identifies the approximately N to the three-halves query regime as uncovered and relevant to the four-round attack.
citation_labels: F. Betül Durak et al., Breaking the FF3 Format-Preserving Encryption Standard over Small Domains
